title: basic-auth pre-flight checks the secret key before the admin bootstrap
answers: admin user created before secret key validated
where is basic-auth bootstrap password checked at startup
body:
Invariant: in mlflow/server/__init__.py:_bootstrap_basic_auth, get_flask_server_secret_key() must run before bootstrap_admin_user().
The secret-key check is cheap and has no side effects, so a misconfigured server fails before the admin user is created or the bootstrap password is validated.
If the order is swapped, a server with no secret key can still create the admin user and then fail, leaving state behind on a run that never starts.
The docstring of _bootstrap_basic_auth describes both checks as one fail-fast step; keep both inside it.
applies: Edits to the basic-auth pre-flight in mlflow/server/__init__.py.
says: A misconfigured server startup creates an admin account in storage before crashing.
Starting the service without required server secrets leaves behind a created administrator user.
Prevent creating the administrator account if the authentication secret key is missing.
Server startup should fail immediately on missing secrets without altering the user database.
search: In mlflow/server/__init__.py:_bootstrap_basic_auth, get_flask_server_secret_key() must execute before bootstrap_admin_user() during basic-auth pre-flight. Applies to edits in mlflow/server/__init__.py to ensure misconfigured servers fail before creating the admin user or validating bootstrap passwords, preventing lingering database state. Both checks must remain together inside _bootstrap_basic_auth as a single fail-fast step.
